title: Listening and Following Instructions
introduction: Learn about listening and following instructions through simple examples and practice.
definition: An instruction tells us what to do. Listen carefully before acting.
rules: Ask an adult to say the instructions aloud. Listen before looking at the text.
Follow one instruction at a time, then try two instructions in a row.
Use movement, objects and classroom situations to practise.
Ask a grown-up to read: Stand up. Sit down. Clap your hands.
Listen and do each action in order.

vocabulary.description: Put your hand or finger on something.
Turn to face the other way.

examples.question: An adult says: Point to the window. What should you do?
steps: Find the window and point at it.

examples.question: An adult says: Pick up the pencil. What should you do?
An adult says: Stand up, then turn around. What comes first?
An adult says: Touch your nose, then clap. What comes last?

exercises.question: Which means shut the door: close or open?
Which means use your eyes: look or listen?
Which means pay attention to sound: listen or jump?
In 'Sit down, then clap', what comes last?

summary: An instruction tells us what to do. Listen carefully before acting.
